column1: # units.tsv — controlled vocabulary of units, unit conversions, and yield bases used across
# fermdb's measurement tables (PLAN.md C.6 `measurement.unit_as_reported` / `unit_si`, and
# `basis`).
# docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md "Units and quantities" is binding here:
#   * "The declared unit is the only authority. A quantity's scale is never inferred from its
#     numbers." This file exists so a unit conversion never has to be reinvented ad hoc in code —
#     conversions are looked up here and applied explicitly, never assumed.
#   * "value_as_reported and unit_as_reported ... are never overwritten or converted in place.
#     Conversions write value_si alongside, with the conversion rule recorded." A `conversion` row
#     below is that recorded rule.
#   * "basis is mandatory on any yield ... Where the source does not state it, basis is NULL and
#     the value is not usable for cross-study comparison." The `basis` rows below are that
#     vocabulary, taken verbatim from PLAN.md C.4/C.6.
#   * "Ethanol % v/v <-> g/L conversion uses a stated ethanol density and is recorded as a
#     derivation, not applied silently." — the two ethanol `conversion` rows below are exactly
#     that record, extended to isobutanol per this project's own product list.
# Columns:
#   entry_type      unit | conversion | basis — which kind of row this is
#   code            for entry_type=unit: the unit symbol. For entry_type=conversion: "<from> ->
#                   <to>". For entry_type=basis: the basis keyword from PLAN.md C.6 `basis`.
#   from_unit       source unit of a conversion, or 'NA' (not applicable to this row's entry_type)
#   to_unit         target unit of a conversion, or 'NA'
#   factor          multiply a value in from_unit by this to get to_unit, or 'NA' if not
#                   applicable, or 'unknown' where no fixed factor exists (see the OD600 row)
#   factor_basis    the physical quantity/assumption the factor rests on (e.g. a stated density
#                   and temperature), or 'NA' for a fixed dimensional conversion, or 'unknown'
#                   where the conversion is fundamentally not fixed
#   applies_to      'general', or a specific product's YAA:PRODUCT id when the conversion is
#                   substance-specific (e.g. a density-based g/L <-> %v/v pair)
#   description     plain-language explanation
#   evidence, confidence   per docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md "Curation"
# Evidence-honesty pass (this revision, following the compartments.tsv D1 rewrite): every row
# below that was 'high' solely on the strength of citing another fermdb file (PLAN.md,
# docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md, a source module, or another vocabulary TSV) has been changed to
# 'unverified' -- citing an internal document is citing memory with an extra hop, not an
# independent check. A row stays 'high' only when its evidence names something actually checked
# outside the repo in this session (e.g. a ChEBI lookup via web search). The confidence vocabulary
# is closed and has four values everywhere ('unverified', 'low', 'medium', 'high'; D2);
# 'unverified' means asserted but never checked against a source, distinct from 'low' (checked,
# weak).
entry_type
column8: description
column9: evidence

column1: unit
column8: Mass concentration, one thousandth of g/L. Added 2026-09-20: the low-titre isobutanol literature reports in mg/L as a matter of course (22 +/- 1 mg/L for a wild-type control in 10.1186/1475-2859-12-119), and without it every such value had to be recorded with unit 'unknown' -- which would have claimed the unit was unreadable when it was printed plainly.
column9: PLAN.md W.11: phase 1 loads real data by hand to find schema gaps while they are cheap. This one was found on the second extraction -- the low-titre isobutanol literature reports in mg/L routinely (22 +/- 1 mg/L for a wild-type control in 10.1186/1475-2859-12-119), and without the unit every such value had to be filed as 'unknown', claiming the unit was unreadable when it was printed plainly. A naming decision, cited internally like every other unit row here, so 'unverified' like them.

column8: Deliberately NOT given a default factor. An OD600-to-dry-cell-weight conversion is only valid with a calibration curve recorded for the specific strain and spectrophotometer/path length used; applying a generic "fixed g/L per OD unit" rule from memory would be exactly the silently-inferred scale docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md forbids.

column9: Definitional SI decimal prefix (milli = 1e-3), asserted from background knowledge and NOT checked against an external source in this session.
